newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of April 21, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Adobe Systems Inc is introducing PostScript 3 this week at the Seybold Seminars conference in New York, in what is a major step forward in the evolution of enterprise printing, PC Week reported April 21.

Sun Microsystems's JavaSoft unit and Microsoft Corp are racing to provide developers with the most comprehensive, low-level object technology for building distributed Web applications, PC Week reported April 21.

COMPUTERWORLD - Microsoft Corp plans to hold a "scalability day" to demonstrate its forthcoming clustering and enterprise class options for its Windows NT operating system, to quell critics that say Windows NT lacks the processing power to be enterprise server software, Computerworld reported April 21.

The laptop market is taking off in opposite directions - on the low-end with an ultra-ultra portable computer and on the high-end with heavy-duty desktop replacements, called luggables, Computerworld reported April 21.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Compaq Computer Corp has held acquisition talks with direct vendors Micron Technology and Gateway 2000 despite assurances from company chief Eckhard Pfeiffer that the company will not change to a direct-sales model, CRN reported April 21.
The talks and rumors has led to confusion among end-user customers and the channel, causing a potentially explosive reaction from the channel, CRN said.

INFOWORLD - The price of a personal computer with Intel Corp.'s 166-MHz Pentium MMX chip could drop by $400 this fall as the manufacturer pushes faster versions of the microprocessor, InfoWorld reported April 21.
Oracle Corp's disclosure that it has won support for the network computer from Intel could mark a turning point for Larry Ellison's vision of low-cost, stripped-down devices, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - While Sybase Inc and Informix Corp battle for the No. 2 position in database software, some analysts think both companies will lose as the industry consolidates, Information Week reported April 21.

EE TIMES - Semiconductor executives returned home last week from the National Association of Broadcasters convention with a renewed commitment to the market for digital TV silicon and a resolve to work with leading TV makers on chip development, EE Times reported April 21.
Intel Corp's Intelligent Input/Output architecture got a big vote of confidence from attendees at a PCI conference last week, EE Times reported April 21.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS NEWS - Intel Corp plans to cut prices on its older Pentium chips by as much as 37 percent while Pentium Pro prices will fall only slightly, Electronic Buyers' News reported April 21.
The price cuts will coincide with the expected unveiling of the company's 300-MHz Pentium II late next month.

INTERACTIVE WEEK - Regional bell companies are illegally favoring their own Internet affiliates, according to a growing number of indepedent Internet services providers, Interactive Week reported April 21.

With the unveiling last week of its own proposed method for tagging information pushed to Web desktops, Netscape Communications Corp raised the ante in its latest high-stakes showdown with Microsoft Corp, Interactive Week reported April 21.
